decisions.evidence: Overturn networking -> objects. This is index_resolution_set: the decompile matches vendor/halocea/src/blam/networking/index_resolution_set.c line for line (is_initialized==1 guard, |key| % number_of_slots slot, chain walk, local_object_index==-1 -> unlink + push onto entry_free_list + decrement slot/table counts, else update in place, else pull from free list calling add_pool when empty). The sibling index_resolution_initialize in the same CEA family preserves the original source path literal D:\Projects\code\HCEX\sources\objects\index_resolution.c - the owning file is objects\index_resolution.c, an objects object file, not networking. CEA's folder split (get/set filed under networking; initialize/shutdown/remove_local_index/add_entry_to_free_list under objects) is CEA's own per-function guess and is contradicted by that path string. Address layout agrees: a small separate .obj linked between damage.c (ends 0x4f0464, 204-byte gap before 0x4f0530) and objects.c (0x4f06d0+). Being called only from the networking message-delta wrappers 0x4e9c20/0x4e9cd0/0x4e9d40 is use, not residence - those wrappers are the field_translated_index_* layer and correctly stay networking.

Overturn networking -> objects. index_resolution_get, the read half of the same objects\index_resolution.c table as 0x4f0530 (exact match to CEA index_resolution_get.c: is_initialized and -1 guards, |server_object_index| % number_of_slots, chain walk on entry->server_object_index, return entry->local_object_index else -1). It moves with its file. Its 35 callers span slices 02/03/04/06/08/12 and are the per-object-type network delta encoders living in effects/game/items/units/objects (nearly all also call FUN_4ec940); a server-object-index -> local-object-index table consumed that broadly is an objects-owned shared table, and the CEA source path pins the file under sources\objects\.

Overturn networking -> objects. add_pool for the same table: GlobalAlloc(8) for an index_entry_pool node linked into table->entry_pool_list (+0x14), GlobalAlloc(600) = 50 index_entry records of 12 bytes, each initialized to {-1,-1} and pushed onto table->entry_free_list (+0x10) - matches index_entry / index_resolution_table in vendor/halocea/src/headers/. Sole caller 0x4f0530; same object file objects\index_resolution.c.

Overturn networking -> objects, but for a different reason than the other three: it is not part of the index_resolution table at all. Body is a 3-component barycentric-style blend, out = base + (p1-base)*w1 + (p2-base)*w2 over float[3] - a file-local placement helper. Its only caller is FUN_004f2550 (object create/placement, high-confidence objects run, which also calls 0x4f0730/0x4f0900/0x4f2ff0), and it is byte-contiguous with 0x4f0730 (ends 0x4f0727, 9 bytes of alignment padding). So the real seam is: index_resolution.c = 0x4f0530-0x4f06c8, objects.c starts at 0x4f06d0. Not math: a static helper with one in-file caller, not a shared vector routine.

notes: The 0.45-confidence 'networking' island 0x4f0530-0x4f06d0 dissolves entirely; all four functions are objects, but for two different reasons. 0x4f0530/0x4f05e0/0x4f0620 are a separate small object file, objects\index_resolution.c (server->local object index hash table with pooled free list), linked between damage.c and objects.c and consumed by the networking message-delta layer. 0x4f06d0 is the first function of objects.c itself. Decisive evidence is the source-path literal D:\Projects\code\HCEX\sources\objects\index_resolution.c preserved in the CEA build of index_resolution_initialize. Suggested boundary edits to assign_08.json: change the 0x4f0530 note to 'objects: separate object file objects\index_resolution.c, server->local object index hash table used by the network delta layer', and move the 'back to objects (object list/lights/placement)' boundary from 0x4f0730 to 0x4f06d0. The wrappers 0x4e9c20/0x4e9cd0/0x4e9d20/0x4e9d40 are unaffected and remain networking.
